paper.title: Atmospheric Parameter Determination of RR Lyrae Stars With Mephisto Multi-band Photometry
paper.abstract: Phase-resolved atmospheric parameters of pulsating stars, including RR Lyrae stars and Cepheids, are essential for studying stellar structure and pulsation physics and for establishing accurate stellar benchmarks for Galactic structure and assembly history. We present a photometric framework that simultaneously infers Teff, log g, and [Fe/H] from Mephisto multi-epoch, multi-band (u, v, g, r, i, z) photometry. A supervised neural-network forward model is built by training on synthetic colors derived from theoretical stellar atmosphere models. It reproduces the synthetic colors to a precision of 0.01 per cent. The model is applied to observed multi-epoch colors to derive phase-dependent atmospheric parameters. We apply the method to six RRab and four RRc stars in three globular clusters observed with Mephisto. We find typical per-phase uncertainties of about 62 K in effective temperature (Teff), 0.10 dex in surface gravity (log g), and 0.16 dex in metallicity ([Fe/H]). Repeated measurements across the pulsation cycle reduce the typical formal uncertainty of the final [Fe/H] estimates to roughly 0.03 dex. A sensitivity analysis indicates that the five Mephisto colors provide distinct and complementary constraints on the three stellar atmospheric parameters: (u-v) provides robust constraints on log g, (v-g) is informative for estimating [Fe/H], and (u-v), (v-g), (g-r), (r-i), and (i-z) all provide information on Teff. The results demonstrate that Mephisto multi-epoch, multi-band photometry can deliver precise, cost-effective phase-resolved atmospheric parameters for RR Lyrae stars, offering an efficient way to construct large samples of stellar benchmarks for studies of stellar pulsation physics and Galactic structure and evolution.

paper.title: The Non-Relativistic Limit of Five-Dimensional Boson Stars and Scale Invariance Violation
paper.abstract: We investigate the non-relativistic limit of spherically symmetric boson stars in (4+1)-dimensional general relativity (GR). In this limit, the resulting Newtonian theory exhibits an exact scale invariance, leading to a critical boson star configuration with a fixed global U(1) charge and vanishing binding energy. We identify the origin of these properties in the restored scale symmetry and analyze how relativistic and gravitational corrections break this symmetry. By comparing the full (4+1)-dimensional Einstein-Klein-Gordon system with the Wick-Cutkosky model, we quantify the effects of these corrections on the energy-charge relation and the kinematic stability of the configurations. Our results demonstrate how weak violation of scale invariance lifts the degeneracy of the non-relativistic solutions and determines the behavior of boson stars away from the critical limit.

paper.title: Episodic Plasma Flows and Coronal Brightenings in an Arch Filament System Observed with SUNRISE III
paper.abstract: Emerging flux regions (EFRs) transport magnetic flux and release energy in the solar atmosphere, often hosting arch filament systems (AFSs). We present high-resolution observations of an EFR obtained with Sunrise III, combining the Tunable Magnetograph (TuMag), the Sunrise Chromospheric Infrared Spectro-Polarimeter (SCIP), and the Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO). The dataset follows an AFS continuously for nearly four hours. Line-of-sight (LOS) velocities derived from the Mg I b$_2$ line reveal three episodic plasma-flow events, with downflows reaching approximately 17 km s$^{-1}$ at the footpoints and enhanced upflows near the loop tops. Although this pattern agrees with the classical emergence and draining scenario, the strongest upflows and downflows occur nearly simultaneously. Atmospheric Imaging Assembly (AIA) observations at 304 and 171 Angstrom reveal transient extreme-ultraviolet (EUV) brightenings in the surrounding emerging system. Some occur during enhanced-flow episodes, while others do not, indicating that the temporal correspondence is not systematic. Multiline spectropolarimetric inversions reveal temperatures between approximately 4000 and 10,000 K and a smooth variation of magnetic field inclination along a representative AFS loop. Non-force-free-field extrapolations provide the large-scale magnetic context of the low-lying AFS loops and surrounding coronal structures. Together, the observations reveal a spatially and temporally complex evolution without establishing a direct causal connection between local plasma-flow enhancements and EUV brightenings.

paper.title: Exact Rotating Wormholes in Five Dimensions and Their Exceptional-Point Instability
paper.abstract: We give an independent closed-form construction of rotating five-dimensional Ellis--Bronnikov wormholes with equal angular momenta and analyze the radial instability of the reflection-symmetric family. The nontrivial coupled metric equations reduce exactly to an open $A_2$ Toda system. The general two-ended solution is expressed in terms of elementary Toda tau functions; the symmetric subclass reduces to a particularly simple one-parameter family interpolating between the static wormhole and the extremal equal-spin Myers--Perry geometry. On this exact background we revisit the cohomogeneity-one perturbation problem. Besides the ordinary unstable mode of the static wormhole, rotation renders the descendant of its non-normalizable zero mode normalizable. The two purely imaginary unstable frequencies coalesce at $|J|/A=0.100628$, where their eigenvectors coalesce as well, identifying a second-order exceptional point. Beyond it the pair continues as $ω_\pm=\pmω_R+\mathrm iω_I$ with $ω_I>0$: the apparent loss of the radial instability found in the original real-eigenvalue treatment is therefore not stabilization, but a transition to an oscillatory instability. We follow this branch deep into the rapidly rotating regime, where its growth rate becomes strongly suppressed.

paper.title: Resonance correction to time-dependent finite-size effects in Effective Field Theory of binary black hole inspiral
paper.abstract: General Relativity predicts that black holes lack an internal structure and that their tidal Love numbers vanish. However, if astrophysical black holes were instead ultra-compact objects (UCOs) with internal structure, their tidal Love numbers would no longer vanish. Then, during a binary inspiral, their tidal deformation could transfer orbital energy to the UCO, increasing the orbital period and leaving an observable imprint on the phase of the emitted gravitational waves. As we discussed previously, the effect is enhanced if one binary companion is resonantly excited. Here we use the point-particle effective field theory framework to calculate this enhancement. We consider circular orbits and focus on excitations of the internal electric quadrupole, modelling the UCO spectrum as a harmonic oscillator spectrum. However, our methods could be straightforwardly extended to more complicated situations. Integrating out the internal quadrupole induces a series of time-dependent finite-size operators with specific numerical coefficients, which we calculate. We find that the static electric quadrupole Love number $k_2$ is negative, and that all finite-size terms are proportional to $k_2$. We further show that resonant excitation induces a leading 2.5 Post-Newtonian term, compared with the 5 Post-Newtonian term in the time-independent case. Our results confirm the expectation that resonant excitation during a binary inspiral offers one of the best ways to detect whether astrophysical black holes can undergo tidal deformation and, if they do, learn about their internal excitation spectrum.

paper.title: Black Hole Spin Evolution in Magnetized Accretion Flows
paper.abstract: Black hole (BH) spin grows as accretion supplies angular momentum and decreases as magnetically driven jets remove it, driving the BH toward an equilibrium spin, $a_{\rm \star; eq}$. Existing estimates of $a_{\rm \star; eq}$ rely on general-relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (GRMHD) simulations with fixed BH mass and spin, and cover only the extreme limits of horizon magnetic flux $φ\rightarrow0$ and magnetically arrested disks (MADs), $φ\approxφ_{\rm MAD}$. We evolve the BH mass and spin in long 3D GRMHD simulations of radiatively inefficient accretion flows aligned or anti-aligned with the BH spin. We find the spin-up parameter as a function of BH spin and $φ/φ_{\rm MAD}$, and derive the equilibrium spin as a continuous function of flux, $a_{\rm \star; eq}(φ/φ_{\rm MAD})$. The equilibrium spin falls steeply with flux, from $a_{\rm \star; eq}\approx0.9$ in weakly magnetized flows through $a_{\rm \star; eq}(φ/φ_{\rm MAD}=0.5)\approx0.5$ to $a_{\rm \star; eq}(φ/φ_{\rm MAD}=1)\approx0.06$ in sustained MADs. In weakly magnetized flows, a slowly spinning BH must accrete at least its initial mass to reach equilibrium, whereas MADs spin down rapidly rotating BHs after accreting less than half of it. However, as the BH grows, the growing gravitational radius and enhanced inflow reduce $φ/φ_{\rm MAD}$, driving disks whose magnetic-flux supply cannot keep pace out of the MAD state and allowing the BH to transition from spin-down to spin-up. The final spin thus depends on both the magnetic flux history and the accreted mass. We discuss implications for a variety of BH-powered engines and provide a subgrid prescription for galaxy-scale simulations and population studies.

paper.title: Testing Extended Exponential Infrared Teleparallel Gravity with CMB, DESI, and PantheonPlus
paper.abstract: We place cosmological constraints on an extended exponential infrared (EExpIR) $f(T)$ teleparallel gravity model using current observational datasets. The extension is characterized by an additional parameter, $b$, which governs the late-time cosmological dynamics. Owing to the existence of two solution branches, phase-space analysis is employed to select the cosmological branch and to establish an appropriate prior range for the new parameter. In this framework, the torsion sector acts as an effective dark-energy component, exhibiting a smooth evolution from a quintessence-like phase to a phantom regime, while recovering the standard cosmological behavior at early times. To constrain the model parameters, we combine early-Universe observations from Planck, ACT, and SPT measurements of the CMB with late-time probes from DESI BAO and PantheonPlus Type Ia supernovae. Using the full dataset, including the SH0ES calibration, we obtain $b=0.573^{+0.016}_{-0.060}$ and $H_0=70.67^{+0.31}_{-0.35}~{\rm km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ at 68\% CL. Model comparison based on Bayesian evidence reveals that the EExpIR $f(T)$ and the $Λ$CDM models are statistically indistinguishable when only CMB data are considered, whereas the inclusion of the full cosmological dataset with SH0ES leads to a weak preference in favor of $Λ$CDM.

paper.title: Infrared spectroscopy of the longest-period Galactic Mira variables from Palomar Gattini-IR: Identification of a candidate thermally pulsing Super-Asymptotic Giant Branch star
paper.abstract: The population of extremely long-period Mira variables in the Milky Way remains poorly characterized. Their rarity and heavy circumstellar obscuration have precluded systematic studies in optical surveys, yet they are expected to trace the most massive stars evolving through the Asymptotic Giant Branch (AGB). We present IRTF/SpeX spectroscopy of the longest-period ($P\gtrsim1000$ d) Galactic Mira variables identified with the Palomar Gattini-IR survey. Twelve of thirteen targets exhibit characteristics consistent with massive O-rich AGB stars. In contrast, one peculiar source IRAS 19552+3142 exhibits i) a large-amplitude ($ΔJ\gtrsim2$ mag) pulsations with $P\approx1060$ d, ii) strong C$_2$ and CO molecular bands indicating C/O$\gtrsim1$, and iii) SiC emission at $\approx11.3\,μ$m in archival mid-infrared spectra. Its spectroscopically confirmed chemistry makes it the longest period C-rich Galactic Mira variable known; together with the rarity of similar objects, this source is difficult to reconcile with standard massive AGB evolution where hot-bottom burning maintains an O-rich surface composition. Instead, its properties may be explained by super-AGB evolution where dredge-out episodes produce a C-rich surface and circumstellar material. Its high luminosity ($M_{[4.5]}\lesssim-10$ mag), red color ($[3.6] - [4.5]\gtrsim2.0$ mag), and high mass-loss rate ($\gtrsim 10^{-4} \mathrm{M_\odot yr^{-1}}$) resemble extreme AGB star progenitors of intermediate-luminosity red transients in nearby galaxies and a known chemically peculiar super-AGB star candidate in the Small Magellanic Cloud. IRAS 19552+3142 may thus provide a rare look at a Galactic super-AGB star in the thermally pulsing phase. Our results motivate improved theoretical predictions and long-baseline infrared searches for these short-lived, dust-enshrouded endpoints of stellar evolution.

paper.title: Unifying energy-entropy bounds in semiclassical gravity
paper.abstract: We revisit bounds on energy and entropy in semiclassical gravity, aiming to strengthen and unify established bounds, in particular the quantum focussing conjecture (QFC) and the smeared null energy condition (SNEC). Both the QFC and SNEC have important applications and are the strongest in their respective hierarchies; however, neither implies the other, nor reduces to the null energy condition (NEC) in the classical limit. To that end, we define a new class of bounds dubbed gravitational energy-entropy conditions (GEECs) that imply both the QFC and SNEC, and reduce to the NEC classically. We construct an explicit family of GEECs by imposing the defining criteria on a broad set of stress tensor bounds, and constrain its remaining parameter space through test cases, in an effective field theory-inspired approach. Our GEECs are powerful candidate bounds on energy and entropy in semiclassical gravity.

paper.title: Elliptic master integrals and the one-loop cosmological wavefunction
paper.abstract: Loop corrections to the cosmological wavefunction involve similar integrals to those required for scattering amplitudes. For the one-loop triangle of a conformally coupled scalar, the master integrals are elliptic, and so the triangle wavefunction coefficient was expected to be elliptic as well. Using a bootstrap approach, we compute this triangle coefficient exactly and show that it is not: the elliptic periods cancel, and the flat-space wavefunction coefficient is a combination of dilogarithms. The cancellation occurs because the residue of the loop integrand on the elliptic sector is a flat-space amplitude, rational in the loop momentum. The one-loop box, by contrast, is not polylogarithmic, even with a single external leg at each site. Its threshold discontinuity involves elliptic integrals, which we also give in closed form. For regular-tetrahedron momenta the periods of a K3 surface enter its loop integrand.

paper.title: Towards constraining cosmology with HI--galaxy cross-correlations from MeerKLASS
paper.abstract: We present an inference of cosmological parameters from the cross-correlation power spectrum between the MeerKLASS 2019 L-band HI intensity maps and the overlapping WiggleZ galaxies at $z \simeq 0.43$. The analysis is intended as a proof of concept to verify that the full pipeline, from the foreground cleaning of the maps to the likelihood analysis, can be applied end-to-end to real data and can return results consistent with the concordance cosmology. The model of the observed power spectrum includes observational effects that are relevant to a single-dish experiment. In the most optimistic scenario in which we hold the astrophysical nuisance parameters fixed, we obtain $H_0 = 65.3^{+5.8}_{-10}\text{ km s}^{-1}\text{ Mpc}^{-1}$ and $Ω_{\text{m}} = 0.44^{+0.12}_{-0.30}$ at the 68% confidence level. We find that sampling the HI amplitude with an informative prior retains most of the constraining power and changes these results by less than 1 sigma. Moreover, using synthetic data, we show that neglecting the observational effects in the model biases the inferred parameters by up to 2.5 sigma and also underestimates their uncertainties. Finally, we show that varying the number of foreground modes removed and the range of scales included changes the inferred parameters by less than 0.5 sigma. These results demonstrate the robustness of our pipeline in modelling HI intensity mapping data, and set the foundation for future cosmological inference with intensity mapping using MeerKLASS and SKAO.

paper.title: Probing the local primordial non-Gaussianity with clustering of FRB dispersion measure and galaxies
paper.abstract: We forecast the sensitivity of a joint fast radio burst (FRB) and galaxy survey to local primordial non-Gaussianity using the full $3\times2$-point statistic: the angular dispersion-measure (DM) auto-spectrum, the DM-galaxy cross-spectrum, and the galaxy auto-spectrum. Local primordial non-Gaussianity imprints a scale-dependent bias on both the free-electron field probed by FRB dispersion measures and the galaxy field. Hence, all three spectra carry information on the local non-Gaussianity amplitude $f_{\rm NL}$. Adopting a DESI-like luminous-red-galaxy sample and an FRB population over 35% of the sky, we forecast $σ(f_{\rm NL}) \simeq 5$ for both $N_{\rm FRB} = 10^4$ and $10^5$ at fixed Planck 2018 cosmology, marginalised over three astrophysical bias parameters $(b_e^0, z_{\rm fb}, b_g^{\rm amp})$. The $f_{\rm NL}$ constraint is robust to marginalising over the six $Λ$CDM parameters $(ω_b, ω_{\rm cdm}, h, A_s, n_s, τ)$ with Planck priors. At these sample sizes, the galaxy auto-spectrum sets the constraint, while the DM sector's contribution grows with the burst count and becomes decisive for the larger samples anticipated in the SKA era, reaching $σ(f_{\rm NL}) \simeq 2$ at $10^7$ bursts.

paper.title: Gravitational field of spinors with torsion and matter$-$antimatter asymmetry
paper.abstract: The conservation law for the orbital plus spin angular momentum of a free Dirac particle in curved spacetime requires that the affine connection has the antisymmetric part: the torsion tensor, which extends general relativity to the Einstein$-$Cartan theory of gravity. In spacetime with torsion, the Dirac equation becomes a nonlinear, cubic equation in the spinor wave function. Under charge conjugation, the nonlinear term changes sign relative to the mass term. A Dirac spinor and its charge conjugate therefore satisfy different field equations. We use the spinor connection formalism to derive the Dirac equation for a spherical spinor in its centrally symmetric gravitational field with torsion. We determine the energy$-$momentum tensor for this spinor and show that the energy contribution from torsion is negative for matter particles and positive for antimatter particles. Consequently, the ground state of a fermion has a lower energy than the ground state of the corresponding antifermion. We also derive the Einstein$-$Cartan$-$Dirac equations for this spinor; they indicate the existence of particle-like soliton solutions exhibiting matter$-$antimatter energy asymmetry.

paper.title: Isospectrality breaking in the axial quasinormal modes of Reissner-Nordström black holes in dynamical Chern-Simons gravity
paper.abstract: We study odd-parity perturbations of Reissner-Nordström black holes in dynamical Chern-Simons gravity. The dCS action is parity invariant because $\vartheta\,{}^{*}RR$ is the product of two pseudoscalars; nevertheless, the pseudoscalar perturbation has odd parity and enters only the axial sector at linear order and so lifts the axial--polar isospectrality of general relativity. We derive the finite-charge couplings between the pseudoscalar and the axial gravitational and electromagnetic perturbations directly from the linearized field equations. Both directions are governed by the radial kernel $(Mr-Q^2)Δ/r^8$, and at nonzero charge the pseudoscalar couples to $Ψ+χΨ_e$, with $χ=2Q/[r\sqrt{(l-1)(l+2)}]$. After diagonalizing the Einstein--Maxwell sector, we compute branch-resolved quasinormal-mode shifts with exterior complex scaling for the photon-sphere modes and Frobenius shooting for the near-extremal zero-damping modes. For the Schwarzschild $l=2$ fundamental mode we obtain $β\,δω=-0.7733-0.3946\,i$ (units $M=α=1$). Off resonance, the gravitational-led shift scales as $ζ\,l^3$ at $Q=0$ but as $ζ\,l^2/Q$ at fixed nonzero charge and large $l$. The electromagnetic-led branch becomes exactly degenerate with the pseudoscalar mode at $Q_c=2M\sqrt{l(l+1)+1}/[l(l+1)+2]$, where the pseudoscalar potential coincides with the polar partner of the electromagnetic-led potential; there the breaking is $\mathcal{O}(\sqrtζ)$, $M|Δω|\simeq2.4\sqrtζ$ for $l=2$, and the shift reverses sign across $Q_c$. Near extremality the photon-sphere shifts remain finite, whereas the non-degenerate fundamental gravitational-led zero-damping mode is suppressed, $δω/ω\simeq6.0\times10^{3}\,ζ\,(1-Q^2/M^2)$ for $l=2$.

paper.title: Bosonic Dark Matter Cores Can Screen Scalar-Tensor Gravity
paper.abstract: We examine the observational viability of scalarized fermion-boson stars (FBSs) in massless Damour-Esposito-Farèse gravity, using the MPA1 nuclear equation of state and a self-interacting complex scalar field playing the role of an ultralight bosonic dark matter model. Constraining stellar models within a multi-messenger-motivated mass-radius window, we obtain three main results: First, bosonic dark matter acts as a catalyst for spontaneous scalarization. Second, energetically favored configurations are scalarized FBSs featuring bosonic dark matter cores that reconcile strongly coupled regimes with radius bounds. Third, dark matter cores tend to suppress scalar charges, which mimics the effect of a massive gravitational scalar field and could contribute to evade observational constraints. Additionally, the exclusive prediction of scalarized FBSs at high masses suggests a way to test this theoretical scenario.

paper.title: Fermion-Boson Stars in Scalar-Tensor Gravity
paper.abstract: In the massless Damour-Esposito-Farèse scalar-tensor theory of gravity, we numerically construct static, spherically symmetric star models composed of a mixture of fermionic and bosonic matter, interacting purely gravitationally. The fermionic sector is modeled as a perfect fluid, while the bosonic sector is described by a massive, free, complex scalar field. We demonstrate that mixed fermion-boson stars can undergo spontaneous scalarization, and we systematically investigate the role played by the bosonic field across different regimes of bosonic mass, central fermionic pressure, and central bosonic amplitude. Our analysis reveals a complex interplay among the parameters, giving rise to a variety of scalarized configurations, ranging from fermionic matter embedded within extended bosonic halos to bosonic cores confined within fermionic matter. We examine sequences of solutions, in particular mass-radius surfaces, and we determine the critical coupling parameter for the onset of scalarization.

paper.title: Constructing likelihoods for a non-Gaussian gravitational-wave background
paper.abstract: The stochastic gravitational-wave background from stellar-mass compact binaries is non-Gaussian since it is made up of a finite number of individual mergers. Over the years, several methods have been developed to search for this background beyond the standard cross-correlation statistic. We reformulate the data analysis problem for such astrophysical backgrounds in terms of the characteristic function of the data in multiple detectors, and show that the existing searches arise as different limiting cases. We also show that new searches can be constructed through different approximations of the characteristic function, which gives a concrete way to engineer suitable approximate sufficient statistics. To illustrate this framework in the context of a simple example, we use the formalism proposed here to analyze an exactly solvable toy model.

paper.title: Unifying stochastic and deterministic signals: a practical search for the intermittent binary black-hole background
paper.abstract: Over the past decade, the Advanced LIGO, Advanced Virgo, and KAGRA detectors have detected nearly 400 compact binary mergers, most of which are stellar-mass binary black-hole (BBH) mergers. Nevertheless, most mergers in the Universe are too weak to be individually detected at current sensitivity levels. Since a BBH merger in band is much shorter than the average time between successive mergers, the population of these subthreshold events gives rise to an intermittent background of gravitational waves (GWs). This GW background is guaranteed to exist, but it has not yet been detected with current stochastic or deterministic searches. Here we propose a fast and accurate likelihood-based search for this background, which unifies the standard model-agnostic cross-correlation search and a fully deterministic, template-based search in a single likelihood. Our search is based on a truncated likelihood ratio, which is fully marginalized over the extrinsic parameters of the individual mergers, and which represents the data in two detectors as an expansion in terms of approximate sufficient statistics. These statistics are higher-order cross-moments of the data, weighted by geometrical factors that generalize the standard overlap reduction function (ORF) used in cross-correlation searches. We show that almost all the Bayesian evidence and information on the BBH merger population comes from correlations between frequency bins induced by individual mergers and is captured in the higher-order generalized ORFs. Consequently, any likelihood function that does not take these inter-frequency correlations into account is necessarily suboptimal. We validate our search on one year of simulated Advanced LIGO data, and find that a catalog-informed analysis, which uses information from both the detected and unresolved mergers, can infer the peak of the redshift distribution of the population of BBH mergers.

paper.title: The coupled evolution of nuclear star clusters and intermediate-mass black holes in a dwarf-galaxy merger
paper.abstract: Nuclear star clusters (NSCs) and intermediate-mass black holes (IMBHs) are expected to coexist in low-mass galaxies and might together facilitate the coalescence and growth of IMBHs. We simulate an equal-mass, gas-rich dwarf-galaxy merger in which each progenitor hosts a $10^3\,\rm M_\odot$ IMBH embedded in a $10^6\,\rm M_\odot$ NSC to study their co-evolution. The simulation model combines the multiphase interstellar medium and fully sampled initial stellar mass function of GRIFFIN at $4\,\rm M_\odot$ gas resolution with the regularised post-Newtonian black hole dynamics of KETJU. Black holes are modelled as accreting sink particles without feedback. Without NSCs, $10^3$-$10^4\,\rm M_\odot$ IMBHs sink only to separations of $50$-$200\,\rm pc$ and capture no gas. With NSCs, the clusters coalesce within ${\sim} 500\,\rm Myr$, the IMBHs form a binary within a few Myr, and scattering of mainly old NSC stars drives them to merger ${\sim} 340\,\rm Myr$ later. The NSCs also promote gas capture, growing the black holes to $1.1\times10^5$ and $4.1\times10^4\,\rm M_\odot$. Gas capture is suppressed during the merger-induced starburst by stellar feedback and the motion of the NSCs relative to the gas, and proceeds in brief supernova-regulated episodes once the NSCs have settled in the centre. Scattering by the IMBH binary and the merger recoil of ${\sim} 175\,\rm km\,s^{-1}$, which removes the remnant from the NSC but not from the galaxy, leave a larger, rotating NSC with a flat core. The stellar tidal disruption rate rises towards coalescence, and the merger is detectable with LISA out to high redshift. NSCs thus remove the delivery and hardening bottlenecks of IMBH mergers in low-mass galaxies.

paper.title: The General-Relativistic Limit of f(R) Gravity
paper.abstract: We establish the general-relativistic limit of f(R) gravity coupled to a massless scalar field for small, asymptotically Euclidean, well-prepared Cauchy data near Minkowski spacetime. We prove global existence and future causal geodesic completeness, with uniform estimates for the metric, matter, and rescaled effective field as an admissible family of modified Lagrangians f(R) approaches the Einstein-Hilbert Lagrangian R. The physical and conformal metrics and the matter field converge to the limiting Einstein-massless-scalar development, uniformly on the entire future spacetime, together with finitely many space and time derivatives. The effective field, defined by a nonlinear reparametrization of the physical scalar curvature, converges to the scalar curvature of the limiting Einstein development. The main analytical difficulty is that the effective-field mass tends to infinity, while its evolution equation becomes an algebraic trace relation. Small field amplitudes may coexist with high-frequency oscillations and comparatively large derivatives, whose quadratic contributions must be controlled uniformly. Using the Euclidean-hyperboloidal foliation method and adapted wave coordinates, we analyze a quasilinear wave-Klein-Gordon system whose nonlinearities do not satisfy the classical null condition. We combine oscillatory estimates, weighted interior and exterior energies, and propagation estimates for the discrepancy from the Einstein trace relation. Quantitative convergence on compact regions and uniform spacetime decay yield global convergence.

paper.title: Rotation and outburst-like brightenings in ZZ Ceti stars observed by TESS
paper.abstract: Context. Pulsating white dwarfs, such as ZZ Ceti stars, allow for the study of white dwarf rotation through rotationally split pulsation modes. Space-based photometry has also revealed outbursts in some cool ZZ Ceti stars.   Aims. We extend the search for rotationally split pulsation multiplets and outburst-like brightenings among known ZZ Ceti stars observed by TESS. We check whether the TESS data add new evidence for a connection between outburst activity and stellar rotation.   Methods. We analysed 120 s and 20 s cadence TESS light curves available up to Sector 96. After light curve correction and quality filtering, we performed iterative frequency analysis. Candidate rotationally split multiplets were identified automatically and visually validated. Outburst candidates were selected from smoothed flux excursions, followed by light curve inspection and pixel-level TESS diagnostics.   Results. We identify 11 ZZ Ceti stars with accepted triplet candidates and derive rotation periods of about 8-94 h; three triplet detections are reported here for the first time. The targets are broadly consistent with the dispersion of rotation periods found in previous studies. The time-domain search produced 19 outburst-like events in 11 stars after light curve inspection. Pixel-level diagnostics indicate that most are likely caused by foreground asteroid contamination. We identify three stars (TIC 219442838, TIC 307908863, and TIC 630426257) as candidate stellar outbursters. None belong to the accepted triplet-rotation sample.

paper.title: Holography and localization in fractional field theory
paper.abstract: Fractional field theory is a promising framework wherein to quantize the gravitational interaction but the presence of nonlocal operators can make its handling difficult. With the purpose of easing this problem, we recast the theory as a local dual in two ways. First, we generalize the Caffarelli--Silvestre extension theorem to self-adjoint fractional field theories with multi-scale kinetic terms and nonlocal interactions, taking the example of a scalar field. The latter is reinterpreted as a nonlocal boundary degree of freedom holographically dual to a local theory of two scalars living in a higher-dimensional bulk. However, inclusion of a local non-linear potential is not straightforward. We therefore propose an alternative picture where the nonlocal theory is not extended to a higher-dimensional space but is localized at the price of introducing a continuum of masses. This \emph{spectral localization} allows for a natural implementation of the fakeon prescription and the related classicization procedure, already employed in local theories with higher-derivative and complex ghosts. Applications to fractional quantum gravity and its comparison with quadratic quantum gravity are discussed.

paper.title: Integrable singularities obstruct Cauchy horizons and mass inflation
paper.abstract: Black-hole interiors with an inner (Cauchy) horizon are unstable through the Poisson-Israel-Ori mass-inflation mechanism, governed by the Dray-'t Hooft-Redmount relation and widely regarded as a dynamical realization of strong cosmic censorship. We show that static, spherically symmetric anisotropic interiors supported by a marginally divergent but integrable density $ρ\sim A/r^2$, with $A>1/(8π)$ and mild screening at finite radius, are incompatible with this mechanism. The compactness $q=m/r$ decreases monotonically from a super-critical central value to $1/2$ at the unique event horizon, producing a strictly positive compactness gap throughout the trapped region and excluding any second zero of the lapse. This gap enters the dynamics quantitatively. (i) Under the null energy condition and a dynamical screening condition, $2m/r$ is non-decreasing along both future null directions of a trapped domain, so the gap propagates under nonlinear spherically symmetric evolution. (ii) For ingoing radiation (generalized Vaidya), the gap bounds the blueshift: the advanced time spent in the gapped region is finite, whereas it diverges at a Cauchy horizon. (iii) For counter-streaming null dust, the radiative part $μ$ of the Misner-Sharp mass obeys exactly $\partial_u\partial_vμ=2\,\partial_uμ\,\partial_vμ/(r|f|)$, of which the DTR relation is the thin-shell form; the in-out coupling $2/(r|f|)$ is uniformly bounded on the interior precisely when the gap is positive. This yields an a priori mass bound and, in the Ori thin-shell model, an e-folding rate bounded by the influx luminosity instead of tending to the inner-horizon surface gravity. Integrable-singularity interiors thus realize a class of sources for which the Poisson-Israel-Ori amplification channel is structurally inoperative in the models in which mass inflation was originally established.

Here we present the matched multi-band catalogue, which integrates photometry and light curve data from all bands, containing photometry for almost 21.7 million Gaia DR3 sources, of which $113\,449$ are identified as variables. We give an overview of the survey's variable content with respect to its main characteristics and known variability type classifications. The comparison with the cross-match catalogue of Gaia DR3 sources with variables from the literature compiled by Gavras et al. (2023) and the International Variable Star Index (VSX) indicates that approximately $40\,\%$ of the variable sources remain unclassified in terms of variability type. Light curves for all of these sources are contained in the GDS data catalogues, available via the German Astrophysical Virtual Observatory (GAVO), and can contribute to their classification.

paper.title: Gravitational Interactions in Nuclear Clocks
paper.abstract: Atomic clocks achieve extraordinary precision through quantum control over large ensembles of atoms, with precision increasing and atom number advancing steadily. Emerging nuclear clock technology encodes clock states in nuclear rather than electronic transitions, offering a new frontier for precision measurement. Here we study whether a large ensemble of such clock nuclei could be used to observe their mutual gravitational interaction. We investigate the gravitational redshift induced by neighboring atoms, including nuclear energy superpositions as sources of gravity, giving rise to a genuinely quantum gravitational interaction between pairs of nuclei. We find that the resulting clock frequency shift due to mutual gravity may become non-negligible for a macroscopic number of nuclei, for instance in a solid-state thorium clock, and we propose approaches to mitigate electromagnetic field effects by exploiting spatial symmetry and high-precision spectroscopy. We further discuss how energy-induced mass superpositions could be directly probed using external gravitational field sensors. By contrast, observing gravity-induced entanglement involving clocks would require substantially greater experimental advances due to decoherence from spontaneous emission. Taken together, our results suggest that nuclear clocks, either alone or in combination with complementary sensors such as optomechanical systems, may offer a future route toward probing gravity at short distances and testing gravitating quantum source masses beyond the Newtonian limit.

paper.title: SuperCrude EoS: A Simple, Analytical, and Reasonably Accurate Equation of State for Astrophysical Fluid Dynamics
paper.abstract: We present SuperCrude, a vastly simplified astrophysical equation of state that captures the most important physics needed for explosive astrophysics, but using compact, physically-motivated analytical approximations rather than precise interpolated data tables. We present a number of code tests demonstrating the performance of SuperCrude in a wide range of parameter space. In large regions of parameter space, SuperCrude is precisely accurate to within the accuracy level of helmeos. For some regions (especially where degeneracy, gas, and radiation are comparable) SuperCrude has errors in its effective adiabatic index on the order of a few percent. The solver's estimate of the temperature is less accurate, on the order of tens of percent. Because the solver is analytic, SuperCrude is designed in such a way to guarantee exact thermodynamic consistency. We incorporate SuperCrude into some hydrodynamic and astrophysical test problems, including the thermonuclear explosion of a white dwarf star. When coupled with a stiff nuclear network, SuperCrude does not achieve the same nucleosynthetic yields as helmeos, motivating future work to improve the temperature accuracy further.

paper.title: A morpho-kinematic view of the Necklace nebula
paper.abstract: We present a morpho-kinematic study of the Necklace Nebula based on spatially resolved spectroscopic observations and 3D modeling performed with the SHAPE software. The nebula is characterized by an equatorial disrupted ring accompanied by bipolar outflows. The geometry and velocity field of these different components are derived from the comparison between observed and synthetic images and position-velocity diagrams. The best model successfully reproduces the main morphological and kinematic features of the nebula, allowing us to constrain its 3D structure. We confirm that the disrupted ring is tilted about 60° from the plane of the sky, but the bipolar outflows are inclined by 46° with respect to the line of sight. This situation might indicate that the bipolar structures are not simple extensions of the equatorial ring, but instead correspond to a distinct mass-ejection event. The slight misalignment between these two components suggests either precession of the ejection axis, a temporal change in the dominant mass-loss geometry, or a misalignment in the magnetic field. Given that the Necklace Nebula hosts a close binary central star and is a well-established post-common envelope planetary nebula, our results support a scenario in which binary interaction plays a central role in shaping its morphology, even before the common envelope phase.

paper.title: Mg II Signatures of Frequency Dependent Wave Propagation in Magnetic Elements
paper.abstract: Waves in solar magnetic elements provide a pathway for transporting and dissipating energy in the chromosphere, yet the relationship between photospheric oscillations and chromospheric spectral structure remains incompletely understood. We investigate whether distinct chromospheric Mg II spectral states are linked to different populations of photospheric kink mode oscillations, with particular focus on the role of high frequency (~5mHz) waves. Magnetic elements are tracked in SDO/HMI magnetograms to derive horizontal velocity power spectra, while corresponding Mg II h + k profiles from IRIS are classified using k-means clustering into morphology-based (SHAPE) and intensity-based (ABS) groups. Both classifications exhibit systematic differences in oscillatory behavior. The SHAPE clusters isolate spectral morphologies associated with enhanced high-frequency power, including cases where oscillations in the 4-6 mHz band exceed those in the photospheric p-mode band. In contrast, the ABS clusters show a monotonic increase in the relative contribution of high-frequency oscillations with increasing emission strength and magnetic flux. These results indicate that high-frequency oscillations are both selectively enhanced in specific chromospheric states and systematically strengthened in stronger magnetic environments. This suggests that magnetic structuring plays a key role in regulating both the transmission and the conversion of kink mode wave energy into observable chromospheric signatures.

paper.title: Gravitational Reconstruction in $AdS_{4}$
paper.abstract: We reconstruct linearized gravitational perturbations in $AdS_{4}$ from a conserved, traceless stress tensor on a fixed conformally flat boundary metric, extending our earlier real Lorentzian construction. For admissible data with no spacelike Fourier support in a flat conformal frame, the physical response reduces to an integral over boundary light-cone cuts. Boundary improvements restore Fefferman--Graham (FG) gauge while preserving normalizability and the linearized Weyl tensor. We then reconstruct perturbations with general spacelike boundary momentum, including nonzero frequency and its zero-frequency limit, using explicit position-space generalized functions on real stress data. Boundary kernels are constructed for normalizable perturbations and sufficient conditions are derived for the reconstruction to converge. The results motivate controlled flat-space limits relevant to Bondi--Metzner--Sachs symmetries and celestial holography.

paper.title: Detailed chemo-dynamical characterization of four elusive Milky Way star clusters
paper.abstract: A variety of faint and observationally challenging stellar systems has been discovered in the Milky Way in the last decades. Unveiling their kinematic and chemical properties is crucial to understand their nature and to assess their role in the history of our Galaxy. In this paper, we present a chemo-dynamical analysis of four elusive stellar systems (BH 140, Garro 01, BLISS 1, and Kim 3) using spectra collected with the X-shooter medium-resolution spectrograph at the VLT. We derived precise line-of-sight velocities and chemical abundances for all targets. Specifically, we provide the first spectroscopic characterization of metallicity and α-element content for BH 140, the first comprehensive chemical characterization for BLISS 1 and Garro 01, and the first spectroscopic metallicity determination for Kim 3. BH 140, Garro 01 and BLISS 1 are relatively metal-rich systems with [Fe/H] ~ -0.7 dex and have enhanced α-element abundances, whereas Kim 3 is notably metal-poor with [Fe/H] ~ -1.8 dex. We also performed an orbital analysis to investigate their origin as accreted or in situ systems. We found that Garro 01 and BH 140 have orbits confined within < 1.5 kpc from the Galactic plane, the former having also a remarkably circular orbit. They were likely born in situ, although the high orbital eccentricity of BH 140 and its mild deficiency in α-elements leave other possibilities open. Although undoubtedly accreted, BLISS 1 does not exhibit a clear dynamical association with any known progenitor, lying in a high energy (E) - high vertical angular momentum (LZ ) prograde orbit reaching a maximum height from the Galactic plane of zmax ~ 8 kpc. Its chemical properties seem to favor an in situ origin, which might be connected with the Aleph sub-structure. Finally, we tentatively link the high energy and low LZ orbit of Kim 3 to the Elqui stream.

paper.title: Probing Scalar Polarization with Next-Generation Gravitational-Wave Detectors: The Roles of Detector Geometry and Source Inclination
paper.abstract: Gravitational-wave observations of compact binaries offer a direct way to test whether gravity admits polarizations beyond the two tensor modes of general relativity. We perform a forecast to assess how well future multi-messenger events will constrain the presence of scalar polarizations in gravitational waves. Performing binary neutron star injections, we forecast next-generation constraints on three modified gravity parameters in the PPE formalism: $α$ (tensor amplitude), $α_B$ (scalar amplitude) and $β$ (tensor and scalar phase). Cosmic Explorer (CE) and Einstein Telescope (ET) each tighten every parameter by 1--2 orders of magnitude over an O5 LIGO-Virgo network, with ET's triangular geometry giving a persistent $\approx2\times$ improvement over 2$\times$CE on the scalar-mode amplitude $α_B$ in both a GW170817-like and a second, representative BNS. We show that, if the sky position and luminosity distance are known from EM observations, adding an EM-based prior on the orbital inclination $ι$ narrows the $α_B$ constraint by $\approx56\times$ relative to an isotropic inclination prior, for a GW170817-like event. We also assess how EM inclination priors as well as assumptions on the neutron star equation of state may affect the inference on the scalar amplitude $α_B$. Overall, these results indicate that detector geometry and the availability of well-placed EM external information are both important levers --- alongside raw network sensitivity --- for next decade scalar-polarization tests.

paper.title: Running cosmological constant in light of recent CMB-BAO data
paper.abstract: We revisit single-field slow-roll inflation driven by a running cosmological constant, i.e. a cosmological constant receiving a logarithmic radiative correction, in light of the latest CMB-BAO data. The relative radiative correction $δ$ is treated as a free parameter of the model and allowed to be positive or negative. For positive $δ$, the predictions interpolate between a logarithmic regime and a linear inflation one. Compatibility with CMB-only data is confined to a narrow stripe near the $2σ$ border where $δ$ is relatively large. On the other hand, the predictions fit easily within the constraints including BAO data in a wide range of parameters. For negative $δ$, the slow-roll approximation breaks down at small field values and the predictions are excluded by data. However, once the effective mass contribution inside the logarithmic correction is taken into account, the negative $δ$ potential develops a local maximum and behaves like a hilltop model, achieving compatibility with CMB-only data, while agreement with CMB-BAO data is possible only at $2σ$.

paper.title: Are Black Hole and Cosmological Horizon Thermodynamics Necessarily Inequivalent?
paper.abstract: It has recently been argued that cosmological horizon thermodynamics and black hole thermodynamics are generically inequivalent in any consistent, UV complete theory of quantum gravity, where it was suggested that this could be falsified by the identification of a counterexample. This conjecture was motivated in part by noting that cosmological horizons do not incorporate many of the convenient features found in the black holes described by string theory. In this work, we consider as a toy model a universe with a single non-rotating black hole and a positive cosmological constant. We work in the Nariai limit where the mass of the black hole is taken to its maximum possible value, and where we also assert that the quantum field theory living on this background is strictly parity invariant. In the semi-classical regime where we neglect instability of the exact Nariai equilibrium under quantum fluctuations, we find that the observer cannot readily distinguish the physics in the neighborhood of the black hole horizon from the physics in the neighborhood of the cosmological horizon. This does not prove that the two are generically equivalent in any universe, though it does suggest that they cannot be entirely unrelated in general. We propose that any consistent theory of quantum gravity that aims to describe black holes in a universe with a positive cosmological constant should provide a related microscopic origin for the leading semiclassical cosmological entropy and black hole entropy in the neighborhood of the particular limit considered here.

paper.title: Early-time tails in Kerr black hole ringdown
paper.abstract: Black hole ringdowns are modelled as a superposition of quasinormal modes (QNMs), although the branch cut of the Green's function produces a nonoscillatory tail that may contaminate early-time ringdown analyses. Within linear perturbation theory, we quantify this branch-cut contribution for the scattering of localised Gaussian wave packets by a Kerr black hole with mass $M$. Defining the onset of ringdown as the earliest time at which the QNM and branch-cut contributions reconstruct the waveform, we evaluate the branch-cut amplitude relative to the QNM amplitude. For wave packets with a characteristic frequency $ω_0\sim 1/M$, the branch-cut amplitude is typically of order $10\%$ of the QNM amplitude at ringdown onset with only a mild dependence on spin. We further find that the tail waveform before convolving with a source is almost independent of spin. The spin dependence of the relative amplitude therefore resides primarily in the excitation of the QNMs. Our results suggest that the branch-cut contribution may affect the accuracy of black hole spectroscopy, particularly near the onset of ringdown.

paper.title: Simultaneous Real-Color Time-Domain Survey of the Coma Field with the Multi-channel Photometric Survey Telescope (Mephisto)
paper.abstract: We present the results from a high-cadence, multi-channel time-domain survey targeting the Coma galaxy cluster, utilizing the newly commissioned 1.6-m Multi-channel Photometric Survey Telescope (Mephisto). Mephisto's pioneering mosaic focal-plane design enables strictly simultaneous imaging in three distinct optical bands ($u/v, g/r, i/z$). This unique capability allows for the extraction of true, instantaneous spectral energy distributions (SEDs) of fast-evolving transients. Our survey continuously monitors a 20-square-degree footprint centered on the Coma cluster. By strategically targeting this massive local structure, we exploit cosmic anisotropy to significantly amplify the volumetric discovery rate of stellar explosions. During the initial six-month pilot operation, we successfully detected and tracked nine new supernovae (SNe). Remarkably, our high-cadence, multi-band strategy allowed us to capture ultra-early rising light curves and pre-discovery signals (e.g., SN 2026dyr) hours to days prior to formal discovery alerts. These instantaneous early-phase colors allow us to reconstruct intrinsic SEDs without temporal interpolation, providing reliable constraints on the physical parameters of early supernova (SN) evolution. Furthermore, our observed supernova yield shows good agreement with theoretical forecasts based on local stellar mass and star-formation rate overdensities. These pilot results validate the efficiency of the Mephisto Coma survey, demonstrating its objective capability to systematically explore the local transient population and provide rapid optical localizations for future multi-messenger events.

paper.title: The Korean Space Telescope (KST): A Dedicated Space Observatory for the Dark Universe
paper.abstract: The Korean Space Telescope (KST) is a next-generation 1.4-meter wide-field space observatory, a dedicated probe of the dark sector. Its single instrument provides diffraction-limited visible imaging (~0.15 arcsec in the optical) together with simultaneous near-infrared (R ~ 100) slitless spectrophotometry, so that every detected source is observed in the NIR by the survey itself, with spectral information delivered at a resolution set by its brightness (full R ~ 100 typing at the bright end, synthetic medium-band or broadband photometry below it) and with no separate follow-up, a capability decisive for time-domain science. With it, KST addresses the three outstanding questions of dark physics in concert: the dynamics of dark energy, the nature of dark matter, and gravitational-wave dark sirens as independent cosmological rulers. KST combines measurements of expansion and structure growth to test dark-energy models. A two-tiered "Wedding Cake" strategy (2,000 deg^2 Wide plus 10 deg^2 cluster-targeted Deep Survey) combines weak lensing, baryon acoustic oscillations, and a near-infrared-standardized Type Ia supernova Hubble diagram to constrain dark energy at its pivot redshift (sigma(w_p) ~ 0.03); maps dark matter from cluster cores to galactic substructure to test cold dark matter against warm and self-interacting alternatives; and builds a deep near-infrared host catalog for a distance-ladder-independent H_0 from dark sirens. The same data yield a Legacy Science portfolio (galaxy evolution, active galactic nuclei, exoplanets, and the Milky Way) at no additional observing cost. As Korea's first dedicated astrophysics space mission, KST occupies a niche complementary to the Vera C. Rubin Observatory, Euclid, and Roman.

paper.title: Complete quasinormal modes of Type-D black holes. II. Extremal Kerr black holes
paper.abstract: We develop a double-confluent Heun (HeunD) method that extends our construction of complete quasinormal-mode (QNM) spectra to extremal Kerr black holes. Matching the horizon-ingoing and infinity-outgoing radial solutions together with angular regularity yields the frequencies directly at extremality, without extrapolation from nonextremal spins. For gravitational perturbations, we obtain an expanded spectrum on both conventional and unconventional Riemann sheets, including additional QNMs revealed by analytic continuation across frequency branch cuts. Continuation in spin connects the extremal modes to our complete Schwarzschild spectrum, including its unconventional branches. We show for the first time that unconventional Class I sequences with $m<0$, continued from unconventional Schwarzschild modes, approach negative superradiant bounds with vanishing damping in the extremal limit. We also identify finite-damping modes interspersed among sequences approaching zero damping, showing that a single overtone cutoff cannot describe the transition to extremality. Independent scattering-amplitude calculations verify representative frequencies and their sheet assignments, while a contour count establishes spectral completeness within a bounded frequency domain. Uniform matching near the superradiant bound further distinguishes critical accumulation from isolated extremal QNMs and resolves the associated Riemann-sheet structure. These results bring extremal Kerr into our unified treatment of black-hole QNM spectra and reveal how the Schwarzschild mode families reorganize in the extremal limit.

paper.title: A Low-Dimensional Chemical Representation of High-Resolution Stellar Disk Spectra: Residual Abundance Signatures
paper.abstract: Stellar abundances are generated by complex chemical enrichment pathways yet show strong correlation structure. We test how well high-quality spectra of low-alpha disk stars can be reconstructed using low-dimensional models. By validating model performance in flux space, we quantify and locate where residual information persists. Using HARPS spectra (R = 115,000, SNR > 100) and labels derived with Korg, we train generative models (The Cannon) conditioned on stellar parameters Teff, log(g), [M/H], vsini, and vmic, and three abundance labels, [Ti/H], [Y/H], and [Nd/H], representing distinct nucleosynthetic families. Evaluating model performance on unseen test stars through flux residuals, the model reproduces the global spectra to a median residual amplitude of 0.3%. Deviations in 15 absorption features for unlabelled elements are typically < 0.7%. Residuals of ~1% correspond to abundance differences of 0.01-0.05 dex. Degrading the spectra to medium resolution (R = 28,000) decreases the median residual amplitude from 0.3% to 0.2%, redistributing the residual signal over the instrumental line profile. Our publicly available model reproduces features from 29 elements to sub-percent precision across -1.13 < [M/H] < 0.29. This demonstrates that the dominant chemical variation encoded in low-alpha disk spectra can be captured by a low-dimensional model, while weaker chemical information remains encoded in flux residuals. High-resolution, high-SNR spectra (R ~ 100,000, SNR > 100) are essential to resolve the hierarchical layers of chemical information beyond this low-dimensional structure. The model provides a benchmark for assessing the chemical information accessible to current surveys like 4MOST and GALAH 2, as well as upcoming facilities like VLT/HRMOS and GMT/G-CLEF.

paper.title: Harmonic brightness oscillations point to magnetar giant flares in rare short gamma-ray bursts
paper.abstract: Kilohertz quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) have been observed in a few rare gamma-ray bursts (GRBs), but their physical origin remains uncertain. We reanalyze the two short GRBs with reported kilohertz QPOs, GRB 910711 and GRB 200415A, and find evidence for possible harmonic-like organization around a characteristic frequency scale near 360 hertz. The similar harmonic-like pattern in GRB 910711 and in the confirmed magnetar giant flare (MGF) event GRB 200415A, including features extending above 4 kilohertz, points to timing phenomenology on frequency scales relevant to magnetar oscillation modes. The temporal and spectral similarities between the two events and the difficulty of explaining these features in merger-driven scenarios favor an MGF-like interpretation of GRB 910711. This timing phenomenology may therefore provide an additional observational handle, complementary to spectral, temporal, and localization information, for distinguishing rare MGF-like transients from merger-driven GRBs.

paper.title: Gravitational lensing of gravitational waves by a Kerr black hole
paper.abstract: We simulate the gravitational lensing of gravitational waves (GWs) by a Kerr black hole using a $(1+1)$-dimensional time-domain mode-sum approach. To enable efficient explicit time evolution, we implement a localized hyperboloidal foliation combined with a static field redefinition, ensuring bounded characteristic speeds across an extended, uniform tortoise-coordinate grid. Incident GW initial data are constructed by projecting a plane-wave Weyl tensor onto the Kinnersley tetrad. Through local spin-dyad rotations and Wigner $D$-matrix transformations, our framework accommodates both idealized wave packets and realistic binary coalescence signals at arbitrary incidence and polarization angles. To accurately resolve the lensed waveforms, we evolve over $68,000$ coupled $(j,m)$ modes. Our results reveal that a Kerr black hole acts as a diffraction-limited thick lens, focusing GWs into a forward beam. For idealized wave packets, the primary prompt pulse exhibits a spin-independent transverse Gaussian profile, whereas the subsequent lensing coda is sensitive to the black hole's spin. For binary coalescence signals, strong-field lensing substantially modifies the post-merger ringdown. However, the lensed inspiral and merger phases in Kerr and Schwarzschild backgrounds are virtually identical, yielding waveform mismatches below $2.2\times10^{-5}$ across various inclinations and polarizations. These findings demonstrate that non-spinning Schwarzschild models provide an accurate and computationally economical surrogate to search for strong-field lensing signatures with current ground-based detectors.

paper.title: XRISM/Resolve Study of Large Scale Properties in Tycho's Supernova Remnant
paper.abstract: Resolve, the microcalorimeter array aboard the X-Ray Imaging and Spectroscopy Mission (XRISM), provides an unprecedented spectral view of Tycho's Supernova Remnant (SNR). We fit the X-ray spectra of the five public archival XRISM observations of the SNR with a multi-component non-equilibrium ionization plasma model assuming spherical expansion and a uniform abundance pattern. For pointings away from the center of the object, we divide each into three spectra based on angular distance from the remnant's geometric center and fit all three simultaneously with the center-pointing observation. We tie elemental abundances together across all model components. We find that pseudo-spherical expansion fits well the Tycho SNR in the regions where Resolve has observed, although iron appears slower on the approaching side than the receding side. We also find that a close-to-uniform abundance pattern across the SNR is consistent with these data.

paper.title: A universal relation predicts the observed reversal of a supernova chirp
paper.abstract: Superluminous supernovae, among the brightest stellar explosions, are thought to be powered by newborn magnetars. One such event, SN 2024afav, ``chirped'', displaying sinusoidal, increasing-frequency ($P(99\textrm{ d})\sim39\pm8$ d to $P(166\textrm{ d})\sim17\pm5$ d) light-curve modulations. The model explaining this chirp, a precessing disk falling onto the dimming magnetar, generalizes to a normalization-independent universal relation between the period derivative and the dimming rate of the light curve. Applied to the published chirp alone, with the spin-down time measured from the unmodulated light curve, the relation predicts that the chirp must halt near $t \approx 150$ d and reverse. With continued follow-up of SN 2024afav, we report the discovery of five new modulations in which the chirp reverses ($P(177\textrm{ d})\sim24\pm4$ d to $P(208\textrm{ d})\sim38\pm2$ d) at $t=147\pm3$ d, as predicted. Applied to chirping events from upcoming surveys, the relation could identify the precession mechanism and disk physics of each engine.

paper.title: Energy-flux noise induced by imperfections of the Gaussian beam in the Li-Baker HFGW detector
paper.abstract: This paper investigates the energy-flux noise induced by imperfections of the Gaussian beam (GB) in the Li-Baker high-frequency gravitational wave (HFGW) detector. Modeling these imperfections with higher-order Laguerre-Gaussian (LG) beams, we analytically derive the resulting noise-to-signal ratio for both co- and cross-polarized $\mathrm{LG}_{nl}$ modes. It is found that higher-order co-polarized LG beams generate no tangential energy-flux noise at the optimal detection plane ($φ=π/2$ or $3π/2$), whereas higher-order cross-polarized LG beams introduce non-negligible noise. Specifically, for an individual higher-order cross-polarized $\mathrm{LG}_{nl}$ mode under our representative parameters, maintaining the noise-to-signal ratio below unity typically requires the power fraction to satisfy $σ_{nl}<10^{-46}$, with the $\mathrm{LG}_{01}$ mode imposing the most stringent constraint of $σ_{01}<6.0\times10^{-49}$. Monte Carlo simulations suggest that the total power fraction $σ_{\mathrm{total}}$ of multiple higher-order cross-polarized $\mathrm{LG}_{nl}$ modes needs to remain below $10^{-49}$. Consequently, we propose employing a polarization filter to retain only the co-polarized component of the GB adopted in the practical experiment, thereby suppressing the noise while preserving signal integrity. These results provide theoretical guidance for noise control in the Li-Baker HFGW detector.

paper.title: Scalar-induced gravitational waves in spatially covariant gravity with two tensorial degrees of freedom
paper.abstract: We study scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs) in a spatially covariant gravity model with two tensorial degrees of freedom, minimally coupled to a $k$-essence scalar field. For the parameter choice considered during radiation domination, the quadratic tensor action coincides with that of general relativity (GR). We derive the scalar transfer functions at finite $σ\equiv C_2\bar N$ and in the large-$|σ|$ limit. We then construct the source function of SIGWs. We further examine a cubic extrinsic-curvature interaction that modifies the source function of SIGWs without affecting the background or quadratic actions. We calculate the fractional energy density of SIGWs for monochromatic and log-normal primordial curvature power spectra. We find that, for the positive values of $σ$ studied, finite-$σ$ effects suppress the spectrum over a broad range of scales relative to the result in the $σ\rightarrow \infty$ limit. In this limit, the cubic interaction suppresses the spectrum at small wavenumbers and enhances it at larger wavenumbers. These results show that modified scalar dynamics and non-linear interactions can alter the fractional energy density of SIGWs even when the quadratic tensor action is identical to that of GR.

paper.title: Insights into the Kinematic Evolution of Filament-Induced Jets: Coupling of Interchange and Flare Reconnection
paper.abstract: Jets are ubiquitous eruptive activities in the solar atmosphere, playing an important role in mass transport, atmospheric heating, and energy supply. However, the triggering mechanism remains elusive. To reveal the fine process of jet evolution, we study a jet associated with a B-class flare that involves in two distinct stages. Analyzing the complete evolution of a solar jet captured by the Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO), we clearly identify its dual-stage kinematics, evolving from interchange to flare reconnection. This dual-stage jet is characterized by distinct dual-stage signatures in magnetic morphology, H$α$ profile, jet speed, jet height, X-ray flux, loop-top source, and temperature. These differences are naturally unified by a physical picture coupling interchange and flare reconnection, offering new insights into understanding of the physical process of filament-induced jets.

paper.title: The seeds and silhouettes of optimal gravitational shielding
paper.abstract: We construct complete vacuum initial data sets with prescribed asymptotically flat exterior geometry, including the gluing of two Schwarzschild exterior regions with small masses (which need not be positive). The construction allows for arbitrarily slow leading decay and nonzero second fundamental form. For leading terms with a fixed radial power, we first construct localized seed data sets whose constraint errors decay to any prescribed finite order, then apply the projection and stability theorems of our companion papers. The resulting vacuum data sets differ from seeds by harmonic terms controlled by Hamiltonian and momentum silhouettes, and by super-harmonic corrections. This difference of harmonic terms is measured by a relative notion of ADM energy-momentum, which is defined even for slowly-decaying data sets that do not admit an ADM energy-momentum. Upon adjusting seed data sets by either harmonic-decaying terms or compact transverse-traceless terms, we freely control this relative ADM charge and, when it exists, the total ADM charge. In particular, when gluing Schwarzschild metrics the total ADM mass can be specified independently of the Schwarzschild mass parameters. Together with our companion papers, these results establish a constructive theory of optimal localization beyond harmonic decay.

paper.title: Radial pulsations of gravitationally decoupled anisotropic self-bound stars with a generalized linear equation of state
paper.abstract: We construct anisotropic self-bound stellar configurations through gravitational decoupling in the minimal geometric deformation framework and investigate their stability against linear radial perturbations. Retaining the Tolman IV temporal potential, we impose the generalized linear equation of state $P_r=η(ρ-ρ_s)$ on the complete matter distribution. Central regularity and Schwarzschild matching determine the radial geometry and relate the surface density to the compactness and stellar radius. Closed-form solutions are obtained for $η=1,1/2,1/3,1/4$, including the MIT bag radial relation when $η=1/3$ and $ρ_s=4B$. Since the equilibrium anisotropy does not determine its dynamical response, we introduce two material prescriptions that preserve either the anisotropy of each fluid layer or its ratio to $ρ+P_r$. Including metric perturbations, we compute the fundamental mode and three overtones for twelve equilibrium configurations under both prescriptions. All 24 background response combinations have positive fundamental squared frequencies, establishing linear radial stability within the adopted closures. The fundamental eigenvalue decreases with compactness within each sampled family, while changing the anisotropic response produces shifts whose direction depends on the background. Tangential tensions in several configurations and the failed tangential profile diagnostic of the maximally stiff family limit their physical interpretation. These results provide analytically tractable self-bound backgrounds and demonstrate that identical equilibrium configurations can support distinct radial spectra depending on their anisotropic material response.

paper.title: Emergence of an acoustic black hole in a lattice model
paper.abstract: We build an acoustic black hole in a lattice model: a draining vortex evolved by the local collide-and-stream rule of a lattice-Boltzmann model, with no acoustic metric imposed, the geometry being measured from the steady state. A horizon emerges, first located from the measured Mach profile and then confirmed by phonon ray tracing on the measured metric, and the ringdown after a perturbation follows approximately the quasinormal frequencies of the draining bathtub. The residual departures are traced to the cell-scale structure of the horizon, which is not an ideal absorber. We model it in two ways: as a reflective horizon on the ideal bathtub, with two free parameters (the modulus and phase of the reflectivity), and as the sonic point of the realised flow absorbing in its own frame, with no adjustable parameter. The second describes the horizon and the non-rotating spectrum best. Superradiance has two ingredients: the emergent geometry, which amplifies in a loss-free calculation on the measured metric, and the horizon, whose absorption frame sets the width and strength of the amplified band but leaves no trace in the ringdown. Both models are used to examine superradiance, which has not been observed in the present toy model: whether the lattice hole superradiates dynamically remains open. The lattice leaves its own imprint as well: a fourfold anisotropy of the sonic surface and a surface gravity set by the cell-scale structure of the horizon.

paper.title: Horizon Residues, Matter-Trace Winding and Test-Scalar Modes in f(Q,T) Gravity
paper.abstract: We extend the analysis of local horizon remnants in quadratic non-metricity gravity to a specific matter trace theory with the functional form f(Q) = Q + alpha Q^2 + 16 pi lambda T. Here, the matter trace is defined by contracting the energy-momentum tensor with the metric from the original matter action. In the absence of explicit lambda-corrections, the theory inherits the vacuum logarithmic-connection hairy branch. To obtain a non-zero trace, we introduce polynomial non-linear electrodynamics and construct an exact magnetic branch in coincident Cartesian Kerr-Schild coordinates. The non-metricity scalar of this branch vanishes, while its matter trace is proportional to the inverse eighth power of the distance. Its metric component function is given by 1 - 2M/r + q^2/r^2 + C/r^6, where the correction term C equals xi(1 - 4 lambda)q^4 / 10. Consequently, the quadratic non-metricity coupling is sterile on this branch. We derive the metric and matter equations, the Euclidean temperature, the single-horizon remnant, the master scalar equation, and the first-order gauge shift. The logarithmic derivative of the matter trace imparts a winding number of -8 on a closed contour enclosing the central singularity, but a winding number of zero on a sufficiently small horizon contour. Nevertheless, the temperature and scalar propagation still vary continuously with the correction coefficient. Therefore, the trace winding number classifies divisor data rather than superseding the matter trace or determining its backreaction. This analysis also demonstrates a degeneracy between the trace coupling coefficient and the non-linear electromagnetic coefficient. These results are specific to this particular branch; this paper does not expound upon the full coupled gravity spectrum, nor does it claim priority for this magnetic metric.

paper.title: The Disk Awakens: IXPE's Sequel Observation of GS 1354-64 Suggests Changing-Look Behavior in the Steep-Power-Law State
paper.abstract: After decades of only failed transitions, the black hole X-ray binary GS 1354-64 has undergone a complete outburst again. We present its first X-ray polarimetric investigation in the fading steep-power-law (SPL) state, following an earlier intermediate-state IXPE campaign during the same outburst. The 2-8 keV emission has a polarization degree (PD) of 2.3 +/- 0.2% and polarization angle (PA) of 5 +/- 3 degrees. Compared with the intermediate state, where PD=3.9 +0.3/-0.2% and PA=-2 +/-2 degrees, the broadband PD is lower while the PA remains consistent. The intermediate-state type-C quasi-periodic oscillation state has also disappeared, marking a major reconfiguration of the accretion flow. Assuming a distance of 7 kpc, the observed the intensity drop from 2.5% to 1.6% of the Eddington luminosity over 10.2 days is punctuated by several broad hour-to-day-scale troughs, tracing two distinct tracks in hardness-intensity space. Simultaneous spectroscopy shows the troughs' spectra contains a cooler disk with smaller apparent normalization, while no change in the Compton component's photon index or normalization is required between tracks. The model-independent analysis identifies a steeper increase in PD with energy outside the troughs, yielding G_E=1.5 +/- 0.2%/keV, compared with G_E=0.7 +0.3/-0.5%/keV during the troughs. Their duration and spectropolarimetric morphology distinguish the troughs from traditional short absorption dips seen in X-ray binaries, providing a possible stellar-mass analog of the recurrent accretion changes that drive "changing-look" behavior in supermassive black hole systems.

paper.title: Absorption of bound supernova axion-like particles by the neutron star weakens the heating limits on their photon coupling
paper.abstract: Axion-like particles (ALPs) that couple to protons are produced in a core-collapse supernova, and the slow ones remain bound to the new neutron star. Bose, Ganguly, Kumar, and Raj [arXiv:2610.30255] proposed that the photons from the decay of this bound cloud reheat old neutron stars, and they derived strong limits on the ALP-photon coupling. They neglected the absorption of the ALPs by the star, but a bound ALP on an orbit that enters the star and reaches 50 km crosses it about $6\times 10^{18}$ times over the 333 Myr age of PSR J2144$-$3933. We show that inverse nucleon bremsstrahlung in the cold star absorbs every ALP whose orbit enters it within minutes, long before it decays, so only ALPs born outside the final star on nearly circular orbits survive; they carry $9\times 10^{-9} - 6\times 10^{-5}$ of the heating. We compute the protoneutron-star evolution, the production, the general-relativistic orbits and the absorption ourselves, for twelve protoneutron-star evolutions, three nucleon-bremsstrahlung rates normalized to the same supernova energy loss of light ALPs, and equations of state with and without $Δ(1232)$ isobars. PSR J2144$-$3933 still excludes a window at $m_a\simeq 7.7-196$\ MeV, with a lower edge in the photon coupling $280-700$ times higher than without absorption. Pion conversion and the $Δ(1232)$ resonance, which raise the production of surviving ALPs more than their absorption, widen this window to $m_a\simeq$ $7.7-260$\ MeV. The window depends at similar levels on the bremsstrahlung rate and on the radius of the final star. It requires a direct photon coupling that cancels the one induced by ALP-pion mixing, and existing supernova gamma-ray limits may already cover it.

paper.title: Robustness-based selection of laser-locking architectures for time-delay interferometry in space-based gravitational-wave detectors
paper.abstract: Space-based gravitational-wave detectors compare laser phases exchanged between distant spacecraft. Offset phase locking keeps beatnotes in the phasemeter band, while time-delay interferometry suppresses laser frequency noise. A disturbance of one reference can degrade the functions that depend on it, making robustness an additional criterion for choosing a phase-reference architecture. We introduce a quantitative comparison based on established cascade equations and percolation measures, with directed reference graphs and Erdős--Rényi support layers. Under uniform disturbances, the robustness score is determined by the reference-depth distribution. Under nonuniform disturbances and partial dependence, the connected-support criterion can select a different configuration from both the published depth and local-lock criteria and a reference-path baseline. The phase-locking comparisons favor configurations that limit accumulated degradation and supply downstream lasers from references retaining greater connected support. Paired finite-network calculations support these differences in preference. In a separate comparison of optical-input support for time-delay interferometry, requiring connected support on all spacecraft gives a different preference from requiring it on at least one spacecraft. These findings identify disturbance location, reference dependence and the required extent of support as factors that can change architecture selection. Within the stated statistical model, robustness rankings can complement phase-locking feasibility and interferometric performance when prioritizing configurations for space-based gravitational-wave detectors.
